column2: You are at the northeastern boundary of a clearing in the midst of a battle-scarred city. The massive wart-like complex in the background is the only thing in sight which appears to contain life.
The structural warpage, and the enormous gaping hole indicate a violent end for this corroding battle machine.
It smells exactly like the hull of a useless, burnt out battle vehicle.
It needs salt.
A very wise choice! Carefully placing the unstable ordnance back inside the tank, you decide some things are better left alone.
The huge building supports miraculously still stand.
You inhale the smell of the column and file it away in your brain under "Useful Information."
Good thing it's not below freezing, or you'd end up spending the whole game with your tongue stuck to the frozen metal.
A battered and boarded purple building stands silently now.
Another of Xenon's ruined structures awaits the the final, slow assault of nature.
The building is inaccessible.
It smells like hundreds of sweaty public servants once populated this building.
It tastes about like you'd expect it to taste, given how it smells.
It's a safe bet that tank had something to do with the end of traffic on this thoroughfare.
The pavement has lost that wonderful wet-tar smell you loved so much as a kid.
Okay, you scrape some taste buds off onto the street.
One thing THIS society can say is that no citizen lives on the streets. In fact, nothing seems to live anywhere. This place is definitely DOA.
The smell of devastation is everywhere.
The taste of devastation is everywhere.
You are at the left edge of this area. More debris chokes off the west.
This is the interior of a battle-scarred tank. A piece of unstable ordnance rests in the corner.
This is the interior of a battle-scarred tank.
Surprisingly, no one has taken this small, innocuous-looking piece of unstable ordnance.
Okay. You now have the unstable ordnance. Remember, it was your idea. Good luck.
Oh No! Sequel Police!
The young shuttle pilot, his seat suddenly humidified by your surprise entry, fires his pulseray.

The shot just misses you and then bounces off the reflective surfaces of the cabin...eventually managing to fatally perforate you. Just as you fade from the living organism club you think, in amazement, "So that's what my spleen looks like!"
Lightning strikes the large wart-shaped behemoth. Its distance away is great enough to demonstrate the travel time difference between light and sound.
This is a landing gear assembly. It currently supports the ship.
You're starting to show your age.
You examine your puny piece of rope and realize that it wouldn't be strong enough to hold this puppy to the ground.
You can't budge this.
This is the landing gear compartment flap.
You see a rubble barrier to the north.
The relatively undamaged building shows no entrances.
A once-prosperous bank building stands partially wrecked and sealed shut.
In the distance not-so-fortunate buildings barely stand in ruin.

You stand centrally located in perhaps the only debris-clear area on the surface of this city. This was a busy intersection of commerce when times were happier and life... well... just existed. An odd structure looms in the distance.
You look at the finely-sculpted ship. It looks to have been designed for atmospheric operation - probably used solely for patrol excursions.
Your pockets aren't big enough.
The dust kicked up by the retros, the heavy stench of burning fuel, and the sharp smell of electricity make for a unique olfactory extravaganza.
You sear your tongue on the hot metal. Apparently it's only safe to touch the now-exposed area beneath the landing gear housing flap.
This seems to be a relatively-spacious landing gear compartment. Wonder how cramped it gets in there when the gear is stowed.
You don't want to put that in there. You might need it later.
This is where those militia-types enter and exit the shuttle.
I think we're looking at your basic surface transportation intersection.
It doesn't exactly smell April-fresh.
It's not as big a taste sensation as other parts of the city.
I would think that something identifiable as UNSTABLE ORDNANCE would be low on your list of fun and healthy things to carry.
Serious damage to important body parts, pretty much screws up any future plans you might have had for living. Bummer!
This grate has crud, gunk, and sludge built up around the edges. You can see through the grate but can't make anything out.
The cool, rank smell of a sewer wafts up from underground.
Okay, you taste grate and find it less filling.
The grate is anchored securely by bolts with mildly corroded heads.
The bolted down grate won't budge.
A battered and boarded storefront shows the wear and tear a little war can inflict.
The building is closed up with welded metal panels.
A large void indicates the absence of any dense matter.
As is so often the case with voids, there is nothing to smell.
As is so often the case with voids, there is nothing to taste.
A fluid-looking mass lying in the gutter is actually crystalized toxic run-off.
It would serve no purpose.
It's probably the most nauseating thing to smell in the whole family of smells.
It's definitely the most nauseating thing to taste in the whole non-liquid liquid family of tastes.
Huge supports miraculously still do just that to these buildings.

You're probably getting bored with these street descriptions so, in an effort to decrease the message tedium to some degree, I won't go into some long description about the grates or the sizeable void to the east. Happy adventuring!
After being away for so long, you'd forgotten how rancid the streets of Xenon smell.
The artificial taste of the Xenon road makes you long for the all-natural flavor of unpaved country lanes.
You are at the eastern boundary of a clearing in this ruined city. Passage to the east is impossible due to a great void in the landscape.
You smell the sidewalk, and it smells back.

You give the sidewalk a lick and accidentally step on a crack. Somewhere, your mother screams out in agony, her spinal cord snapped cleanly in half. Of course, she probably deserved it for the way she threw away those magazines she found in your room that time back in junior high. Those things cost you a lot of good lunch money!
Eeyew! That was a bitter section! I don't think I want to lick the road around here anymore.
The interior of the aircar sports many broken gauges and instruments as well as a glove box.
After taking a quick look around to reassure yourself that the place is as dead as it looks, you snitch the PocketPal(tm) laptop.
It is a closed glove box.
The glove box is empty.
It looks like a genuine PocketPal(tm) portable terminal.
A quick inspection reveals nothing of interest other than a glove box.
The zesty tang of nitroglycerin fills the air around the ship.
It tastes like ship.
This place is a mess. Dangerous terrain prevents travel to the south.
The rubble is too hazardous to attempt passage over.
It smells a little like pebbles and a little like the rubbles.
It tastes like a cement milkshake, only crunchy.
A sidewalk anyone would be proud to own.
This section of the sidewalk still smells fresh after hundreds of years.
There's nothing like fresh air and sunshine to make a sidewalk taste great.
More high-speed travel surface lies useless.
It smells like something that wasn't designed for noses.
This sealed, battered building is the last one standing in the southwestern area.
You are at the southwestern boundary of this chunk of city.
NOW where am I? you wonder aloud to nonexistent auditory organs. This place sure looks homey. Hey, wait! This looks just like Xenon! It IS Xenon! It's.. it's.. it's really a pile.

Along with the changes induced by an armed conflict, the city looks different - more modern with a heavy dash of post-disaster seasoning. Casually glancing at the status line you happen to notice that you're in Space Quest 12!

What's happened? Who was that guy with the overdeveloped hair dryer? Why did you let yourself be talked into jumping into some strange shimmering hole? Why are you talking to yourself? These incredibly intriguing questions will quickly be forgotten with barely an electron stirred in that well-armored orb atop your shoulders.
A twisted and broken expanse of cityscape stretches south from here negating possible travel plans in that direction.
The rubble is rough and jagged. No sense in risking injury this early in the adventure. We'll get to that in due time.
The wreckage left by the destruction of the entire Xenon civilization tastes a little like some ancient ruins you once sampled.
The snappy scent of freshly chopped buildings fills the air.
More rubble can be seen to the north.
Even when you were younger way back in Space Quest 1 you couldn't have pulled that off at this distance.
The direction of the prevailing breezes prevents any hint of aroma.
Decaying and destroyed buildings now house the apparently nonexistent population of Xenon.
A REAL man would actually walk up to a building if he wanted to taste it.
You'll have to be closer to the buildings to give them a really good smell.
You lick a thick smear of filth off the street. Finding the taste unpleasant, you quickly swallow it. What a smart person you are!
You inhale deeply and detect the aroma of very old traffic.
The prevailing noxious wind prevents this.
You are in the southern area of a rare clearing in this destroyed cityscape. Your home as you remembered it does not exist in this period of time. A huge boil of a structure clogs the horizon.
Mmmmmm! Wild Berry!
You take the small, frayed, useless-looking length of rope.
It's a lightweight, worn piece of rope.
Smells like a frayed old length of rope.
You run the risk of tying your tongue in a frayed knot.
The clearing ends here. Progress south is impossible over the jagged terrain.
The rubble is too dangerous for you to mess around on.
The rubble is too dangerous for you to mess with - except maybe for that knotted-looking thing.
The faint aroma of burnt hemp teases playfully around your nostrils.
You swish the rubble around in your mouth a bit, but the flavor is too subtle to identify.
A battered and boarded storefront shows the wear and tear a little war can have on it.
There's a sweet, fruity odor coming from the building.
What looks like fluid is actually a mixture of toxic atmospheric solids.
It smells just as good as it looks.
It tastes just as good as it smells.
The grate is anchored securely by bolts with corroded heads.
It smells grate!
It tastes grate!
It seems to have everything you'd look for in a street with the exception of mobile creatures or vehicles.
The street stinks. Somebody must have been driving on it.
It's very pleasant looking.
It tastes like all the other sidewalks you've ever tasted.
The sidewalk stinks. Somebody must have been walking on it.
A hazardous accumulation of destructured structures blocks safe passage north.

Data Entry 22795: This message is to whomever may be so fortunate as to find it. I am Professor Lloyd, lead designer of the Xenon Super Computer Project, the ultimate in artificial intelligence.
271	From that day forth the possessed computer waged war on the inhabitants of Xenon using our own weapons against us. Some managed to escape to other planets.

Those of us who remained stayed to fight the machines and robots under its control. It was a bloody war. Those of us that were not killed were taken captive and 'modified.'
273	These 'cyborgs' infiltrated the loyal ranks of resistance, rooting out almost all of our hiding places and exposing us to the mechanical menace. Some of these poor souls still wander the streets.

As of this recording, we are down to only a handful of rebels. My health is deteriorating rapidly. To make matters worse, I've just learned that the computer has unraveled the mysteries of time travel.
275	I've sent my two best men to attempt to steal this new technology. If you are not a machine then perhaps they were successful. Please realize - YOU are Xenon's last hope.
